newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Yachting-Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.
newsitem.headline: Australian Yachting-Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.

text.p: By Peter Campbell*
Investor CHARLES CURRAN could be likened to the man who bought a Remington electric shaver and liked the product so much that he bought the company.
In less than two weeks CURRAN will return to the sport of ocean racing in which he enjoyed so much success in the 1970s with a brand new, IAIN MURRAY-designed 60-footer named Sydney.
The yacht has been built by Bashford boatbuilders at the company's plant at Nowra on the New South Wales south coast.

Sadly, the man behind Australia's largest boat-building group, champion sailor IAN BASHFORD, died earlier this year while working on the early construction of this latest production yacht from his company. BASHFORD was only 37.

In Sydney this week his widow, LOUISE, together with MURRAY and CURRAN, announced the establishment of Bashford International Pty Ltd, bringing together Bashford Boatbuilders, the Kookaburra Group headed by MURRAY and the Capital Investment Group, headed by CURRAN.

The company will operate under the name Sydney Yachts by Bashford International, continuing production of the well-established Sydney-36 and Sydney-41 International Measurement System (IMS) racer and cruiser/yachts, the new Sydney-60 IMS cruiser/racer, and a new Sydney-46, all designed by Murray.
It will also continue its active development of the sports sailor, the Magic-25, and the Hobie Cat range.

The first Sydney-60, a comfortable but fast pilot house version built for CHARLES CURRAN, will be launched at Kiama on the south coast in a week or so and will have its first offshore racing in the Telstra Cup, starting on December 27. MURRAY will be at the helm.
PETER GILMOUR GETS HIS REVENGE
Looking out from my office at Rushcutters Bay on Wednesday I could see some real action on the harbour in a match race between the old Kookaburra 12-metres still owned by MURRAY and PETER GILMOUR.

The old 12-metres are still a grand sight but it was not until that evening that I found out that the opposing helmsmen were the two America's Cup stars, providing an exciting day on the water for their corporate customers from Australian Air Express.

GILMOUR, fresh from the international match racing circuit's latest events in Japan (where he won the Nippon Cup) and New Zealand (where he bombed out in the Steinlager Cup), won the day five races to one.
TOP IMS RACERS IN TELSTRA CUP TUNE-UP
The longest running sponsorship of a yachting event in Australia, the Bruce & Walsh Regatta conducted by Middle Harbour Yacht Club, comes to an end this weekend.

JOHN WALSH, a Sydney jeweller and sailing enthusiast, is closing down his city business and it will be with more than a touch of sadness that he presents the trophies after the four-race series' offshore events.
The Bruce & Walsh Regatta is one of the most prestigious events leading up to the Telstra Sydney-to-Hobart, and JOHN will see a fine line-up of IMS yachts racing on the Manly circle.

PETER GILMOUR will be at the helm of Zoe, the considerably revamped Murray-41 owned by Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron member IVAN WHEEN, hoping to lift the yacht's performance after the spring racing in Queensland in which it did not sail up to expectations.

The regatta has attracted a fleet of more than 70 yachts, including all the top IMS racers in Sydney such as GEORGE SNOW's maxi Brindabella, SYD FISCHER's 50-footer Ragamuffin, SEA, the former Tasmanian Mumm-36 now owned by advertising man STEVE KULMAR, DAVID FULLER and HUGO VAN KRETSCHMAR's 36-footer, Bashful, and RAY STONE's new Mount Gay-30, Razor's Edge.
Also there will be the Victorian yachts Atria, to be sailed by designer ROBERT HICK, and Aero Boy, a new Cape-35 owned by Sandringham yachtsman HARRY HERTZBERG.

Maglieri Wines, the Jutson-43 owned by Adelaide medico GEOFFREY VERCOE, has also entered, while former Hong Kong-based WARWICK MILLER, now living in the up-market Sydney suburb of Vaucluse, will be sailing his vivid green-hulled and appropriately named Reichel/Pugh 66-footer Exile.
TASMANIANS TUNE UP IN MARIA ISLAND RACE

There was plenty of time to enjoy the odd tot of the sponsor's product last weekend when the Royal Yacht Club of Tasmania (RYCT) conducted its major local ocean race, the 180-miles race around the East Coast to Maria Island and return. It took the 50-footer Cyclone, owned by Hobart yachtsman STEPHEN KEAL, nearly 36 hours to sail the course, followed home by ROGER JACKMAN's Dr Who and Intrigue, skippered by RYCT past commodore DON CALVERT.

One of the smaller yachts in the fleet, the J-35 Southern Cross Television, skippered by GREG PRESCOTT, won under both IMS and Performance Handicap System ratings on corrected time underlining expectations that the boat will again be a strong contender in the Sydney to Hobart.
Double Image, another Sydney-to-Hobart entry from Tasmania skippered by GREG WILLIAMS, placed second on IMS. Third went to Intrigue.
ENTRIES CLOSING FOR SYDNEY TO HOBART

Five o'clock this afternoon is the official closing time for paid-up entries for the Telstra Sydney-to-Hobart, with nominations passing the 100-mark earlier in the week but back to 98 with several withdrawals.
The withdrawals include Rager, which has been sold by Cruising Yacht Club of Australia commodore and Arnott's Biscuits marketing executive, PETER BUSH.

Also out is Rapscallion, the ex-Cuckoos Nest which won the 1993 race, and PL Lease Future Shock, which had also been entered in the 25th Melbourne-to-Hobart by owner PETER HANSEN. The Elliott-55 is heading to Hobart around the West Coast as originally planned.
FREMANTLE 8 WINS IN HONG KONG
Australian-designed and built yachts continue to do well in regattas in southeast Asia, with a fine performance last weekend by the Fremantle 8 in Hong Kong's Round-the-Island Race.
Sailing in a fleet of nearly 250 yachts, the brand new Fremantle 8, owned by PHIL and VANESSA ELVIS, won the overall trophy by nearly 15 minutes, also placing first in her division.
Chairman of the Perth-based Fremantle Yachts, ANDREW THORPE, and skipper JOHN ROBERSON, flew to Hong Kong to help the owners tune up their new boat, and then sail in the race.
In a fickle and shifty breeze, the Fremantle 8 quickly picked its way to the front of the fleet, hitting the lead soon after the halfway stage of the race.

Although finally overtaken by some of the larger 40 to 50-footers as they neared the finish line off the Royal Hong Kong Yacht Club, the Fremantle 8 still finished eighth across the line and a comfortable handicap winner.
*Peter Campbell is editor of Offshore Yachting magazine.
